## F11.packaging-format — Packaging format

Definition: Manifest and directory layout of a plugin or extension.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] A plugin is a directory of components, usually with a manifest: a JSON file at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` giving its name and optionally a version, a description and other metadata. Claude Code loads a plugin without a manifest; inside the file, only `name` is required. A plugin bundles skills, hooks, subagents and MCP servers as a single installable unit. | ev: E-claude-code-12328, E-claude-code-12371, E-claude-code-09469
- codex-cli [supported, verified] The plugin manifest is a metadata file that identifies a plugin and points to bundled skills, connector mappings, MCP servers, hooks, and metadata. By default Codex looks for `hooks/hooks.json` inside the plugin root. A local marketplace root directory contains `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. A plugin can include apps, skills, or both. | ev: E-codex-cli-01707, E-codex-cli-04013, E-codex-cli-00769, E-codex-cli-02771
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] A plugin is a bundle of components in a single installable unit. An extension lives in its own subdirectory, which must contain an entry file named extension.mjs, extension.cjs, or extension.js; the CLI runs the entry file directly with Node.js. The marketplace.json file is the only required component of a plugin marketplace. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01447, E-copilot-cli-01646, E-copilot-cli-02555

## F11.component-types — Component types

Definition: What a package can ship: commands, agents, hooks, MCP, skills.
- claude-code [partial, verified] Plugins add skills, agents, MCP servers and more; the Claude Security plugin adds one command, `/claude-security`. | limit: Agents shipped in a plugin honor a subset of the subagent fields. | ev: E-claude-code-07657, E-claude-code-06963, E-claude-code-06842
- codex-cli [supported, verified] A plugin is a reusable package that can include apps, skills, or both. A connector is a plugin component linking Codex to data and actions in an external service, and a plugin that needs an MCP server connection prompts you to connect it. App-server `plugin/read` (under development) returns bundled skills, apps, and MCP server names. | ev: E-codex-cli-02771, E-codex-cli-01680, E-codex-cli-01991, E-codex-cli-00240
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] Plugins can deliver preconfigured customizations such as skills, hooks, custom agents, and MCP servers; custom agents are *.agent.md files in agents/. LSP servers included in a plugin are automatically available when the plugin is installed. Extensions add your own tools and slash commands using the SDK that ships with the CLI. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01734, E-copilot-cli-01448, E-copilot-cli-01782, E-copilot-cli-00025
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] Agent plugins install multiple related customization types as one package and can bundle MCP servers. A skill distributed through a plugin gets the plugin name as an automatic command prefix (for example, `/my-plugin:test-runner`). - cursor [supported, verified] Plugins package rules, skills, agents, commands, MCP servers, and hooks into distributable bundles. Skills and MCP servers are supported by both Agent Plugins and Cursor Plugins. | ev: E-cursor-03457, E-cursor-00516, E-cursor-04272
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] Extensions package items including prompts, MCP servers, custom commands and themes. ## F11.install-sources — Install sources

Definition: Where packages come from: marketplace, git, path, archive.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] Claude Code registers the official marketplace `claude-plugins-official` the first time a developer starts an interactive terminal session, downloading the catalog from `downloads.claude.ai` and, if that fails, cloning it from `github.com`. The Agent SDK `plugins` option loads custom plugins from local paths. `claude plugin` manages plugins from the CLI. | ev: E-claude-code-06569, E-claude-code-00989, E-claude-code-07000
- codex-cli [supported, verified] `codex plugin` installs, lists, and removes plugins from configured marketplaces. Marketplaces can be defined in system, cloud-managed, user, or trusted-project config.toml; `marketplace/add` adds a remote plugin marketplace. For the Codex Security plugin, `--plugin-path` takes a plugin directory or ZIP to override the bundled plugin. | ev: E-codex-cli-01158, E-codex-cli-00768, E-codex-cli-00237, E-codex-cli-02265
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] Plugins can be installed directly from a repository, from a plugin marketplace, or from a local path; direct installs also work from owner/repo, a URL, or a local path. ## F11.versioning-update — Versioning and update

Definition: How versions are pinned and updated.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] A plugin manifest can add a version. `/reload-plugins` reloads all active plugins to apply pending changes without restarting. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the plugin's persistent data directory, for dependencies and state that should survive plugin updates. | ev: E-claude-code-12328, E-claude-code-07293, E-claude-code-10011
- codex-cli [supported, verified] A marketplace can optionally pin a Git branch, tag, or commit, and `--ref` pins a Git ref. `marketplace/upgrade` refreshes a configured Git marketplace, or all configured Git marketplaces when you omit the name. - copilot-cli [partial, verified] copilot plugin update NAME updates a named plugin; --all updates all installed plugins at once. Plugins in a marketplace are versioned. ## F11.trust-signing — Trust and signing

Definition: Review, signing and policy controls on installs.
- claude-code [supported, verified] Admins can restrict which marketplace sources users can add and install from. A marketplace's name places it in one of three tiers (official, community, third-party), and Claude Code accepts the official and community names only for marketplaces sourced from `github.com/anthropics/` repositories. Anything a plugin runs, it runs as the user. | ev: E-claude-code-00129, E-claude-code-12585, E-claude-code-12338
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Admin requirements for plugin marketplace sources take effect when `restrict_to_allowed_sources` is `true` and reject unmatched marketplace add and plugin install operations. When the plugins requirements table is present, plugin-bundled MCP servers without a matching plugin and server entry are disabled. A plugin doesn't automatically trust its hooks; Codex skips plugin-bundled hooks. | ev: E-codex-cli-03041, E-codex-cli-03501, E-codex-cli-03040, E-codex-cli-04018
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] A plugin or marketplace pinned by organization or MDM managed policy can't be re-enabled, disabled, or repointed locally; the managed value wins. Pinning to a sha (a full 40-character commit SHA) gives reproducible installs immune to force-pushes or tag/branch moves. Extensions run with your privileges, and the docs advise loading only trusted extension code. | ev: E-copilot-cli-03783, E-copilot-cli-03844, E-copilot-cli-01645
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] The first install from a new marketplace shows a trust prompt to review the marketplace source. `ChatStrictMarketplaces` is an allowlist of plugin marketplace sources: only matching marketplaces are trusted, and an empty array blocks all. Docs advise reviewing plugin contents and publisher before installing, since plugins can include hooks and MCP servers that run code on your machine. | limit: `strictKnownMarketplaces` restricts plugin installation to the listed sources. It does not retroactively disable already-installed plugins. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-01499, E-copilot-vscode-01183, E-copilot-vscode-02832, E-copilot-vscode-01451
- cursor [supported, verified] Marketplace plugins are manually reviewed before listing, must be open source, and each update is reviewed before publishing. An extension install cooldown defers installs and updates until a version has been public for a set number of hours, with optional signature verification. A plugin containing a blocked MCP server installs normally, but the blocked server cannot make calls. | ev: E-cursor-03467, E-cursor-03067, E-cursor-04425
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] `security.allowedExtensions` is a list of regex patterns for allowed extensions; if nonempty, only matching extensions are allowed, and it overrides the blockGitExtensions setting. The install `--consent` flag acknowledges security risks and skips the confirmation prompt. An `admin` setting, when false, disallows extensions from being installed. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00324, E-gemini-cli-01321, E-gemini-cli-00720
- grok-build [supported, unverified] The [plugins] enabled setting takes name lists to explicitly enable plugins (project plugins may default off). | ev: E-grok-build-00214
- grok-bot [supported, verified] If you use Grok Bot through a Cursor team, your Cursor team admin controls which marketplace plugins are available; a disabled plugin needs the admin to enable it. Any connector permitted in Teams Marketplace is available to every Bot a member runs. | ev: E-grok-bot-00515, E-grok-bot-00445
